newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Omega Pharma in 102.7 mln bfr cap increase - BBL.
newsitem.headline: Omega Pharma in 102.7 mln bfr cap increase - BBL.

text.p: Pharmaceuticals firm Omega Pharma is offering 65,000 freely transferable new shares at 1,580 Belgian francs to the public as part of a capital increase, Banque Bruxelles Lambert said on Wednesday.
The issue is worth a total 102.7 million francs.

The 65,000 shares represent 12.4 percent of the existing capital after the increase. In the case of oversubscription there is a green shoe of 30,684 existing shares, representing six percent of the capital after the increase, on offer from majority shareholder Couckinvest NV.
Subscriptions open on June 12 and close on June 27.
Omega Pharma develops and sells cosmetics and dietary products, supplies pharmacies with basic chemicals and sells over-the-counter drugs.
A BBL spokesman said the firm had 1996 sales of 270 million francs and profit of about 15 million francs.
He said the Courtrai-based company was valued at 808 million francs. It has a staff of 35.
There were vague plans for a bourse listing at a later date, he said.
The money raised would be used in the first place to buy licences, to develop new products and for future expansion. Retained profits would also be used for growth.
"The considerable increase in profits expected for the coming years could allow the company to pay a dividend in the next year," the BBL statement said.
Couckinvest, held by founder Marc Coucke, owns 70 percent of the capital. Dutch venture capital firm Halder has about 25 percent, while the remainder is owned by several pharmacies and staff.
